MultiDbError.doc: Single failure channel for multi-database catalog operations. The `kind` field is one of the named conditions listed in master.md pin 15; `message` is human-readable for tests and logs. Targets map MultiDbError to their idiomatic error type while preserving the discriminant.

SchemaIdx.doc: Index of a slot in the catalog's current slot list. NOT stable across catalog_detach (slots above a removed slot compact downward). Callers MUST re-resolve via catalog_resolve at statement boundaries; see master.md pin 11.

AttachSeq.doc: Monotone never-reused index assigned to a slot at catalog_attach time. Used to determine the unqualified-resolution walk order. A fresh attach after a detach gets a fresh AttachSeq strictly greater than any previously issued value.

SchemaSlot.doc: One catalog slot. Owns its own Pager and WalState (the WAL is absent for memory-only schemas). External callers must not introspect; constructors are gated through the catalog.

DbCatalog.doc: Per-connection multi-database catalog. Owns the slot list, the master-journal state machine, and a per-connection RNG for master-journal naming. Single-threaded ownership: targets that wrap multiple connections must instantiate one DbCatalog per connection.

BusySnapshot.doc: Executor-supplied open-cursor / open-statement count per slot. Used by catalog_detach to enforce the busy-guard (master.md pin 12). Index by SchemaIdx; entries beyond the current slot list are ignored.

CommitOutcome.doc: Returned by catalog_commit. dirty_slot_count is how many slots took part in the commit; used_master_journal indicates whether the 2PC path ran (true iff dirty_slot_count >= 2); master_journal_path is present only on the 2PC path and is the absolute path to the journal file that was created and then unlinked.

DbCatalog.name: catalog_open_main
DbCatalog.doc: Open or create the main database at main_path; bind a fresh anonymous TEMP schema in slot 1. Drives master-journal recovery if a stale `<main_path>-mj*` file is present. Returns the catalog with two slots ready for unqualified resolution.

DbCatalog.name: catalog_attach
DbCatalog.doc: Open db_path as a fresh slot under schema_name. Validations in order: (1) catalog must be idle (no in-flight transaction); (2) schema_name (case-folded) must not already exist; (3) slot count < MAX_ATTACHED_DBS; (4) db_path must be openable. On success, a Pager and a WalState are constructed for the new slot, attach_seq is assigned monotonically, and the slot is appended.

DbCatalog.name: catalog_detach
DbCatalog.doc: Remove the slot named schema_name. Validations in order: (1) catalog must be idle; (2) schema_name must NOT be 'main' or 'temp'; (3) slot must exist; (4) busy.open_cursors_per_slot[idx] MUST be 0. On success: checkpoint the slot's WAL, close it, close the pager, drop the slot. Slots with higher index compact down; attach_seq does not change for survivors.

DbCatalog.name: catalog_resolve
DbCatalog.doc: Look up the SchemaIdx of schema_name (case-folded ASCII compare). Returns SchemaNotFound if not bound. Result is valid until the next catalog_detach.

DbCatalog.name: catalog_walk_unqualified
DbCatalog.doc: Return SchemaIdx values in the canonical unqualified-resolution order: main (slot 0), temp (slot 1), then attached slots ordered by AttachSeq ascending. Used by /parts/compiler/parts/qualified-names to drive first-hit-wins lookup.

DbCatalog.name: catalog_begin
DbCatalog.doc: Mark the catalog as in-transaction. write_txn = true reserves the writer for every slot lazily on first write; false opens a read-snapshot. Subsequent catalog_attach is rejected until commit / rollback.

DbCatalog.name: catalog_commit
DbCatalog.doc: Commit the in-flight transaction. If exactly one slot is dirty, single-slot fast path: commit that pager / WAL directly. If two or more are dirty, run the master-journal 2PC: allocate `<main_path>-mj<8hex>` from the catalog RNG, write absolute paths of every dirty slot's per-slot journal, fsync, commit each per-slot journal in turn, then unlink the master journal. Returns CommitOutcome describing what ran. On I/O failure mid-2PC the master journal stays on disk and the next catalog_open_main runs recovery.

DbCatalog.name: catalog_rollback
DbCatalog.doc: Roll back the in-flight transaction across every dirty slot. Idempotent if no transaction is in progress.

DbCatalog.name: catalog_slot_count
DbCatalog.doc: Return the number of currently-bound slots, including main and temp. In the range [2, MAX_ATTACHED_DBS].

DbCatalog.name: catalog_close
DbCatalog.doc: Close every slot's WAL (checkpointing first per /spec/durability.spec.md), close every pager, and free the catalog. Idempotent.
